Transition-Sensitive RANS Modelling of Boundary-Layer Separation on NACA Airfoils at Low Reynolds Number

A validated 2D study with k–ω SST and γ–Reθt closures — OpenFOAM v2412 · Re = 105–106 · α = 0–18° · URANS verification subset

1 · Motivation & Physics

Separation onset limits maximum lift and drives the drag rise near stall on small-UAS and wind-turbine sections.

∂Ui/∂xi = 0   ·   Uj∂Ui/∂xj = −(1/ρ)∂p/∂xi + ∂/∂xj[ν(∂Ui+∂Uj) − u′iu′j]
  • Closure: k–ω SST (Menter) — best-in-class for adverse pressure gradients; γ–Reθt repeats for transition physics
  • Profiles: NACA 0012 · 2412 · 4412 (analytic, 638 pts)
  • Mesh: polar O-grid, y⁺ ≈ 0.4, farfield 20c, 34k cells
  • Solver: steady SIMPLEC, fully turbulent, Tu = 0.1%

2 · Method Pipeline

  • Analytic NACA 4-digit geometry → structured O-grid (serration/tubercle variants retained as 2D negative control, Appendix D)
  • Structured O-grid generator → Gmsh v2.2 → gmshToFoam
  • 123 scripted OpenFOAM cases (core + full Re sweep + grid + 45 γ–Reθt transition repeats + 10 low-Re validation + 2 URANS)
  • Forces, Cp, Cf, separation from wall shear reversal
  • Primary validation: Sandia SAND80-2114 (Re-matched, Re = 3.6×105, free transition); NASA TMR datasets qualitative only (Re mismatch 3–6×)

4 · Separation & Stall

Separation detected from sustained Cf < 0: attached to α = 10°, x/c ≈ 0.20 at α = 15°, with a five-fold drag rise.

5 · Interactive Velocity Field (α = 15°)

6 · Conclusions

  • Pre-stall lift matches tripped experiment within ≈ few % (MAE); drag biased high by the fully turbulent assumption — quantified and consistent.
  • Camber orders maximum lift: 4412 > 2412 > 0012; stall softens with camber.
  • Lowering Re from 106 to 105 cuts lift and raises drag at fixed incidence; the stall-angle shift is muted by the fully turbulent closure.
  • γ–Reθt transition repeats (45 cases, full factorial, identical grids): attached-range drag −2–26% (grows as Re falls), laminar separation bubbles at x/c = 0.06–0.75 that the fully turbulent model cannot produce; near stall the closures diverge (ΔCL −32% to +30%) as bubble burst reshapes separation.
  • Low-Re validation vs Sandia free-transition data (Re = 3.6×105): transition closure cuts attached drag error by 33%; but bubble-burst stall (measured at α = 10–12°) is missed by both steady closures — modelled low-Re stall is an upper bound.
  • Passive devices as a 2D negative control (Appendix D): serrated TE and tubercle surrogate results confirm that both device classes need spanwise (3D) physics — 2D RANS cannot assess them.
  • URANS verification subset (pimpleFoam, α = 12°/15°, Re = 3.6×105, Co ≤ 20): time-averaged loads quantify the unsteady contribution to the near-stall steady-RANS discrepancy.
AERO-BLS — fully scripted reproducible workflow (scripts 00–10) · OpenFOAM v2412 · Data: NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource, NASA TM-4074, R&M 3726, Abbott & von Doenhoff (1959)
